title: Intrinsic finite coefficient stage data and associator shift compatibility
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a prime l different from D.p, an algebraic closure Ω of Q_l, and any scheme Y. Use the prescribed small finite coefficient models and their conjugated inclusion maps. Let the finite stages, integral and rational scalar transitions, their normalized shift comparisons, exactness, tensor associators and unitors be the existing intrinsic constructions, with the same signatures and data. Then for every E≤L≤M the prescribed scalar associator commutes with the prescribed integral-image-normalized integer shifts. The assertion includes repeated fields and identity inclusions. This node also records the existing finite-stage data relocated unchanged from SfAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients into SfCoefficientStageCore; the original module publicly re-exports them.

source.place: Tensor-generator localization step in the retained common-stage shift clause; abstract version of the rational step of lem-pur-intrinsic-associator-shift-square, without its general-stage specialization.

proof.text: The prescribed small coefficient models and conjugated inclusion maps satisfy identity and composition laws. Thus the composite inclusion used by the scalar associator equals the prescribed E-to-M inclusion (a propositional equality of K-algebra maps, which is why the associator is corrected by the equality-transport isomorphism), including reflexive inclusions and repeated fields.

source.place: statement: the finite coefficient fields of Ω ordered by inclusion and the transition functors K↦K⊗_EL for E⊂L, composed along E⊂L⊂M

proof.text: For each coefficient inclusion, the ordinary-to-completed comparison determines a unique coherent integer-shift structure on the intrinsic integral scalar extension. Its component equation is exactly the normalized comparison required by the finite-stage construction, so the three integral transitions used by the associator carry the prescribed normalized shifts.

source.place: statement: 'it is an exact functor of triangulated categories' (the transition's normalized integral shift)

proof.text: Localizing those normalized integral transitions gives the unique coherent integer-shift structures on the rational scalar transitions, with degree-one components equal to the localized integral components. This identifies the rational shift comparisons in the item with the prescribed integral-image normalization, for every integer and for identity inclusions.

source.place: statement: 'it is an exact functor of triangulated categories' and the rationalized categories of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] (rational transition shift)

proof.text: The corrected integral scalar compositor commutes with these normalized integer shifts by the integral associator lemma for the same finite-field datum, coefficient maps, and equality transport. Its conclusion applies to the reflexive and repeated-index cases as well.

source.place: proof, first paragraph: on integral representatives the composites are identified by the associativity of the completed derived tensor product with O_M

proof.text: Apply the abstract rational associator-shift compatibility theorem to the small coefficient models E,L,M, the three coefficient inclusions and the composition equality of Step 1. Its hypotheses are supplied as follows: the corrected integral compositor commutes with the normalized integral shifts (Step 4); for each of E,L,M the degree-one shift functor of the raw rational stage is the scalar localization of the integral degree-one shift, K↦K[1], f⊗a↦f[1]⊗a, by the definition of the induced shift on a scalar localization; and for each of the three inclusions the degree-one rational comparison at Q K is Q of the degree-one normalized integral comparison at K (Steps 2 and 3). The theorem localizes the integral square and extends degree one to all integers without requiring faithfulness of rationalization; it gives that the corrected rational compositor commutes with the normalized rational shifts.

source.place: proof, first paragraph: 'The levelwise reductions and the rationalization ... commute with this identification'

proof.text: Finally, the prescribed finite-stage associator is the corrected rational compositor followed by equality transport along the coefficient-inclusion composition law. The scalar-extension composition isomorphism is natural and identity-compatible, and the prescribed associator of the item is by its definition exactly this corrected rational compositor for the composition equality of Step 1, so the compatibility of Step 5 is the assertion for it. This proves the stated square for every E≤L≤M, including identity inclusions and repeated fields; the relocated finite-stage declarations are the same constructions with their public re-exports.

source.place: statement: 'the canonical isomorphisms ... of [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition] identify the composite of two transition functors with the direct one'
